idempotency.create_run: insert by stable run id; a retry may reuse only an identical immutable request fingerprint and account config revisions
idempotency.checkpoint_probe_attempts: persist one bounded internal result per run, probe key, and attempt before starting the next probe; retries resume completed work without exposing partial report items
idempotency.upsert_items: one item per run id and item key; retry replaces the sanitized result instead of duplicating it
idempotency.append_observations: observation ids are deterministic per run, probe, round, and sample; conflict is a no-op
idempotency.finish_run: compare-and-set running to one terminal state only for the active claim epoch, an unexpired lease, and no stop intent; replay of the same terminal result is a no-op

nodeDivergenceReasons: Go uses an Asynq ops task instead of keeping the expensive probe lifecycle inside an HTTP request.
Go limits infrastructure retries and resumes from persisted stages; probe business failures are terminal and are not retried by Asynq.
Go keeps public run statuses compatible but makes terminal transitions compare-and-set and immutable.
Go replaces the process-local active-run map with a cross-instance lease plus durable PostgreSQL facts.
Go writes idempotently so task retry or worker restart cannot duplicate items or overwrite cancellation.
Go binds queued work to account configuration revisions so a later credential or endpoint edit cannot be misattributed to an older request.
Go computes bounded token padding in-process and does not copy the Node child-process pool or IPC protocol.
Go treats SSE as an observer of a durable run; disconnecting a browser does not own or cancel the job.
